claims.text: Combining high-throughput DSC with refined CALPHAD can accurately determine melting temperatures and fusion enthalpies and entropies in HEAs.
The combined DSC-CALPHAD method can determine the volume change at melting in HEAs.
The combined method can determine liquid-phase thermodynamic properties in HEAs.
The combined method is efficient or high-throughput across the HEA family.
DSC can record heat-capacity behavior and the onset of incipient melting near the solidus.
DSC provides sufficiently precise heat-capacity and transition data for the proposed quantitative extraction.
Multicomponent configurational entropy can lower liquid Gibbs free energy and depress melting temperature.
Configurational entropy makes a substantial contribution to total alloy entropy.
The intrinsic chemical complexity of HEAs modifies their enthalpy and entropy of fusion.
The proposed CALPHAD framework incorporates configurational-entropy contributions and enthalpic mixing effects with sufficient fidelity for property extraction.
Combining DSC observations with CALPHAD predictions enables extraction of fusion enthalpy, fusion entropy, and volume change at melting.
The entropy-stabilized nature of HEAs makes the combined approach more accurate than traditional DSC or independent CALPHAD analysis.
CALPHAD predictions of transformation temperatures and phase properties in HEAs can be challenging and depend on the extent of assessed lower-order systems.
Traditional DSC with generic models or CALPHAD without DSC calibration typically has larger uncertainties than the proposed combined method.
Slow heating under a controlled atmosphere ensures equilibrium during the measurements.
The approach is expected to perform well for single-phase, compositionally homogeneous HEAs.
Multiphase behavior or phase separation before melting can compromise the accuracy of the approach.
For several HEA systems, the predicted melting and fusion properties and volume changes will agree with independent measurements within ±10%.
The quantitative uncertainty reduction from the combined method varies by HEA system and is not established for highly multiphase alloys.
